prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Companion"]
1: ["Mastering Desktop Pet Controls", "Right-click your companion on the desktop anytime to hide, summon, or open interaction options.", "Right-click pet for main command menu", "Start Desktop Session"]
2: ["Custom Pet Photo Inspector", "Upload a clear photo to ensure your companion renders perfectly on your desktop.", "Use clear lighting with a visible face for best rendering results.", "Upload Pet Photo", "Auto-Quality Inspector Active"]
3: ["Preparing Habitat", "Your pet stays on top of open windows when active."]
4: ["Signing in secures your companion data so your pet never resets across logins."]
5: ["Select Your Desktop Companion Path"]
6: ["Building Desktop Habitat..."]
7: ["Tip: Use the system tray icon to quick-toggle pet visibility or change sound settings."]
8: ["Official Pet Adoption Verified"]
9: ["Connect Your Account to Save Progress", "Sign in securely in one click to store your companion and adoption certificate safely."]
